title: Add Lombok in IntelliJ
answer: To add Lombok in IntelliJ, install or enable the Lombok plugin if IDE support is needed, add the `org.projectlombok:lombok` dependency to the Maven build, reload the Maven project, and verify that annotation processing/compiler support is working by compiling or running tests. The IntelliJ plugin helps the IDE understand Lombok-generated members; the Maven dependency is what makes Lombok available to the build. In a Spring Boot project the Lombok version may be managed by the parent dependency management, otherwise use a compatible explicit version. AeroTopo does not currently require Lombok, so this lesson demonstrates the workflow and then removes the temporary project dependency instead of leaving an unused production dependency.

steps.title: Open IntelliJ Settings
steps.question: Lombok has an IDE-support side and a build-dependency side. Before changing the Maven build, why should you first open IntelliJ Settings and confirm the IDE can understand Lombok-generated code?
steps.question_te: Lombok ki IDE-support side mariyu build-dependency side rendu untayi. Maven build ni marchadaniki mundu IntelliJ Settings open chesi Lombok generate chese code ni IDE ardham chesukogaladani enduku confirm cheyyali?
steps.why: The IDE may otherwise show false errors for generated getters, setters, constructors, or builders even when the Maven compiler can process them.
steps.why_te: IDE ki Lombok support lekapothe Maven compiler code ni process chesina kuda generated getters, setters, constructors leda builders meeda false errors chupinchachu. Kabatti munduga IDE awareness ni verify cheyyadam useful.

steps.title: Install the Lombok plugin
steps.question: The Lombok plugin improves IntelliJ's awareness of members generated during annotation processing. Why is installing or enabling this plugin an IDE concern rather than a replacement for the Maven dependency?
steps.question_te: Lombok plugin annotation processing time lo generate ayye members ni IntelliJ ki ardham ayye laga chestundi. Ee plugin IDE concern matrame enduku, Maven dependency ki replacement enduku kaadu?
steps.why: The plugin helps editor analysis and navigation. The build still needs Lombok on its dependency/annotation-processing path, so IDE support and build support solve different problems.
steps.why_te: Plugin editor analysis mariyu navigation ki help chestundi. Kani build ki Lombok dependency leda annotation-processing path lo undali. Kabatti IDE support mariyu build support rendu veru problems ni solve chestayi.

steps.title: Open the Maven descriptor
steps.question: A plugin alone does not make Lombok part of a reproducible build. Why should the next step return to `pom.xml` before using Lombok annotations in project source code?
steps.question_te: Plugin install chesina matrame Lombok reproducible build lo part avvadu. Project source lo Lombok annotations use cheyyadaniki mundu next step lo `pom.xml` ki enduku vellali?
steps.why: The project build file is shared by local development, CI, and other developers. Lombok must be represented in that build model rather than existing only in one person's IDE.
steps.why_te: Project build file local development, CI mariyu vere developers andariki common source of truth. Lombok oka developer IntelliJ lo matrame undakunda build model lo kuda represent avvali.

steps.title: Add the Lombok Maven dependency
steps.question: Lombok works as a compile-time code-generation dependency. What does adding `org.projectlombok:lombok` to Maven provide that the IntelliJ plugin by itself cannot provide?
steps.question_te: Lombok compile-time code generation dependency ga work chestundi. Maven lo `org.projectlombok:lombok` add cheyyadam valla IntelliJ plugin okkate ivvaleni em build capability vastundi?
steps.why: The Maven dependency makes Lombok available to the compiler and repeatable builds. In a Spring Boot project its version can often be managed by the parent dependency-management stack.
steps.why_te: Maven dependency Lombok ni compiler ki available chestundi mariyu repeatable builds lo kuda same behavior istundi. Spring Boot project lo version parent dependency management dwara manage avvachu.

steps.title: Open the Maven tool window
steps.question: After the build model changes, IntelliJ must synchronize its Maven project model. Why is opening the Maven tool window useful before assuming the new Lombok dependency is already active?
steps.question_te: Build model marchina tarvata IntelliJ Maven project model ni synchronize cheyyali. Kotha Lombok dependency already active ani assume cheyyakunda Maven tool window open cheyyadam enduku useful?
steps.why: The Maven tool window exposes the project's build lifecycle and synchronization state, giving a visible place to reload and inspect the updated dependency model.
steps.why_te: Maven tool window build lifecycle mariyu synchronization state ni visible ga chupistundi. Updated dependency model ni reload chesi inspect cheyyadaniki idi correct place.

steps.title: Reload the Maven project
steps.question: IntelliJ can cache an older Maven model after `pom.xml` changes. Why should you explicitly reload the Maven project after adding Lombok?
steps.question_te: `pom.xml` change ayyaka IntelliJ old Maven model ni cache lo unchachu. Lombok add chesina tarvata Maven project ni explicit ga reload cheyyadam enduku important?
steps.why: Reloading forces IntelliJ to resolve the updated dependency model so editor analysis and build tooling agree about what is available.
steps.why_te: Reload cheyyadam valla IntelliJ updated dependency model ni malli resolve chestundi. Appudu editor analysis mariyu build tooling rendu available dependencies gurinchi same state lo untayi.

steps.title: Inspect resolved libraries
steps.question: A declared dependency is not enough evidence that resolution succeeded. Why should you inspect External Libraries to confirm Lombok appears in the resolved project model?
steps.question_te: Dependency declare chesina matrame resolution success ayindi ani prove kaadu. Lombok resolved project model lo vachindani confirm cheyyadaniki External Libraries ni enduku inspect cheyyali?
steps.why: The resolved view shows what IntelliJ actually obtained from Maven, which is more useful than assuming the declaration was downloaded and indexed successfully.
steps.why_te: Resolved view Maven nundi IntelliJ actual ga em pondindo chupistundi. Declaration file lo undi kabatti download mariyu indexing success ayayi ani assume cheyyadam kanna idi better evidence.

steps.title: Verify the build after Lombok setup
steps.question: IDE recognition can look correct while the real build still fails. Why should Lombok setup be verified with a Maven test or compile goal before the team starts relying on generated code?
steps.question_te: IDE lo Lombok correct ga kanipinchina kuda real build fail avvachu. Team generated code meeda depend avvadaniki mundu Maven test leda compile goal tho setup ni enduku verify cheyyali?
steps.why: A successful Maven build proves the shared build path can resolve and process Lombok, not just the local editor.
steps.why_te: Successful Maven build shared build path Lombok ni resolve mariyu process cheyyagaladani prove chestundi; local editor support okkate proof kaadu.

steps.title: Remove the temporary Lombok dependency
steps.question: A learning demo should not leave an unused library in production. Since AeroTopo currently has no Lombok-based source code, why should this lesson remove the temporary Maven dependency after proving the setup workflow?
steps.question_te: Learning demo production project lo unused library ni vadili pettakudadhu. AeroTopo lo ippudu Lombok-based source code lekapothe setup workflow ni prove chesaka temporary Maven dependency ni enduku remove cheyyali?
steps.why: This keeps the cumulative AeroTopo project honest: we learned the real IntelliJ/Maven procedure without permanently adding a dependency the application does not need.
steps.why_te: Dini valla cumulative AeroTopo project clean ga untundi. Real IntelliJ/Maven procedure ni nerchukunnam, kani application ki avasaram leni dependency ni permanent ga add cheyyaledu.
